paragraphs.text: Quiet gradient tints for every Workspace in DeepSeek Harness, a sidebar that reads as a tree, and a
green row for a chat that finished unread.
# Workspace Tints
A quiet colour code for Workspaces in DeepSeek Harness — plus a green row the moment a chat finishes
r code for Workspaces in DeepSeek Harness — plus a green row the moment a chat finishes without you.
Source · npm · veduis.com
## What it does
**One tint per Workspace.** Every Workspace takes a tone from a single warm-to-cool ramp of tinted w
hites — never a saturated accent. The tone washes the Workspace header and draws a 2px rail beside e
ach of its Sessions, so five open projects read as five sections instead of one long list.
**A tree, not a list.** Workspace names are set as section headings (15px, semibold, with air above
them); their Sessions indent beneath in a smaller size (13px). The rail stays at the row edge, so it
reads as the group's spine while the contents step in.
**A green row for finished chats.** When a Session finishes while you are elsewhere, the whole row t
akes a green gradient — the exact green of the status dot that already turns for it. Green is the on
e colour the Workspace ramp never uses, so the two signals can't be confused. The row clears the mom
ent you open the chat.
| Dark | Light |
**You can turn the volume down.** Settings → *Workspace tints* shows every Workspace's current tone
and switches the intensity between **Soft**, **Whisper**, and **Off**. The hierarchy and the finishe
d-chat green are structural signals and stay on; only the tint intensity is switchable.
## Install
From a shell:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or in the app: **Plugins → Install**, and give the package name `dsh-workspace-tints`. Reload the pa
ge if your profile does not use HMR.
It is also listed in a plugin market index, so Discover can install it without typing a package name
: add `https://veduis.github.io/dsh-workspace-tints/index.json` as an index source (Plugins → More →
Custom plugin markets → Discover → Add index source).
Requires a DeepSeek Harness build satisfying `engines.dsh` (currently `^0.2.1-rc.5`). The package is
a bundle: `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one `workspace-tints` row, whose Client half is the stylesheet
and the Settings section.
## How a tone is chosen
The tone is keyed by the Workspace's canonical folder path and remembered in `localStorage` (`dsh.wo
y the Workspace's canonical folder path and remembered in `localStorage` (`dsh.workspace-tints.v1`):

- renaming a Workspace keeps its tone;
- adding a Workspace takes the tone **farthest** from the one
s already in use, so existing Workspaces never change colour and new ones never sit on a neighbour's

hue;
- the ramp holds twelve tones at one lightness (`oklch(0.62 0.052 <hue>)`) and skips the whole

green band;
- deleting and re-adding a folder restores its old tone.
Sessions outside every Workspace stay neutral.
One migration note: assignments made before 1.0.0 are re-anchored to the green-free ramp by nearest
hue, once, on first load.
## What it touches
The plugin owns one `<style>` element plus the Settings section. It reads Workspace metadata through
the public `ctx.workspaces` Client service and never reads another plugin's state. Rows are address
ed by the sidebar's own `data-row-key` identity (`workspace:<id>`, `session:<id>`) and the status do
t's `data-state="done"`; if a future client version renames those, the affected effect stops applyin
g and nothing else changes.
No network access, no telemetry, no analytics. The only persisted state is the tone map and intensit
y in `localStorage`.
## Compatibility
| DSH | Plugin |
The client APIs used (`ctx.workspaces`, `ctx.slots`, `ctx.locale`, `ctx.effect`, `ctx.provide`) are
stable in that range. A wider range will be declared once verified against a newer runtime.
## Uninstall
**Plugins → Workspace Tints → Remove**, or:

The stylesheet and Settings section are disposed with the bundle. The stored tone map stays in `loca
lStorage`, so reinstalling restores the same colours.
## About the screenshots
The images above are rendered from the plugin's own CSS against the shipped theme tokens. The Worksp
ace and Session names in them — Aurora Studio, Lighthouse Ops, Paper Kite, Foundry Labs, Cedar & Co
— are invented for the demo.
